explanation: In C++, virtual member functions enable runtime polymorphism by allowing derived classes to override base class methods. When a function is declared as virtual in a base class, calls to that function through a base class pointer or reference invoke the derived class's overridden implementation, facilitating dynamic dispatch. This mechanism is fundamental for designing flexible and extensible object-oriented systems where behavior can vary depending on the actual object type at runtime.
keywords: virtual functions, runtime polymorphism, dynamic dispatch, function overriding
